dimension_justifications.soundness: Within the deliberately narrow assumptions, the proofs for T1--T3 are self-contained and appear to establish the displayed product/contraction statements: T1 derives the eigencoordinate product and log remainder (paper.tex:88--124), T2 integrates the explicitly pointwise Loewner bounds before applying the norm bound (136--189), and T3 iterates the stated conditional expectation (200--229). This does not establish soundness or relevance outside those premises, and the paper expressly disclaims such transfer (21--32, 191--195, 231--233).
dimension_justifications.presentation: The scope table, theorem statements, and repeated boundary statements make the limited claims unusually easy to identify (44--63). The paper is readable and the supplied build record reports a deterministic, visually inspected five-page PDF. However, its central framing is an exposition of disconnected calculations rather than a research problem with a contribution, so the presentation cannot make the work decision-ready as an ICLR research submission.
dimension_justifications.contribution: The submission explicitly states that it makes no novelty claim (21--32), that no theorem connects its three state spaces or consequences (44--49), and that it remains a scoped exposition rather than an established research advance absent a direct-antecedent distinction, unifying theorem, or empirical evidence (272--275). The closest-work matrix likewise supplies contextual sources only and records no verified theorem-level antecedent comparison (closest_work_matrix.md:10--27). Thus there is no identifiable new knowledge or capability on the present evidence.

paper_summary: This theory-only note proves three separately scoped facts: a fixed-SPD-quadratic product/log-remainder identity (T1), gradient-descent parameter-error contraction under pointwise Hessian bounds on each actual minimizer-to-iterate segment plus a conditional directional refinement (T2), and an affine scalar conditional-mean product law (T3). It deliberately makes no comparator-path, empirical, deployment, or novelty claim.
strongest_verified_contribution: A careful claim boundary: the manuscript gives short self-contained derivations and explicitly prevents the three elementary-looking identities from being read as results about nonlinear SGD, data attribution, unlearning, or neural-network training.
strengths: The assumptions and non-claims are explicit. In particular, T2 prints the full pointwise ambient Hessian premise used by its proof, rather than implying a nonlinear or comparator-path conclusion (paper.tex:136--195).

The manuscript and evidence package distinguish active formal claims from withdrawn empirical material; the claim-evidence map registers only C-THEORY-001 through C-THEORY-003 as active theory claims and labels the empirical claims withdrawn (claim_evidence_map.tsv:2--8).

The active citations are documented as contextual rather than being used to imply novelty, and the closest-work matrix explicitly warns that a locked citation is not a novelty finding (closest_work_matrix.md:3--6).
questions: What precise direct optimization or stochastic-recursion antecedents do T1, T2, and T3 improve upon, and what statement remains true that those antecedents do not already provide? Please give a source-verified, theorem-by-theorem comparison rather than an absence-of-search argument.

If the three results are intended to be one ICLR contribution, what common formal object, nontrivial theorem, or application consequence connects them? If none exists, why should three explicitly disconnected scoped identities be evaluated as a research paper rather than a pedagogical note?

issues.observed_evidence: The abstract says the package makes no novelty claim. Related Work says the locked sources do not provide a verified theorem-level antecedent comparison and consequently does not claim any individual identity or juxtaposition is novel. The closest-work matrix repeats that the absence of a locked antecedent is not novelty evidence and states that the novelty ceiling remains.
issues.why_it_matters: Truthful disclaimers prevent overclaiming, but they also leave the submission without a demonstrated distinction from the established optimization and stochastic-recursion literature. The cited works are explicitly contextual rather than direct theorem antecedents. Consequently, the current package does not identify a new result or capability for ICLR, which is decision-driving even if every displayed derivation is correct.
issues.required_fix: Establish a research contribution, not merely a safer wording. Perform a source-verified comparison against direct antecedents for each theorem and either prove a nontrivial result that is distinct under a meaningful broader scope, or explicitly reposition this as a non-research expository artifact rather than an ICLR submission. A citation list alone is insufficient.
issues.verification_test: For every proposed headline theorem, an independent reader can inspect a direct antecedent matrix with exact assumptions and conclusions, reproduce the claimed logical difference, and see a theorem or result in the manuscript whose content is not already supplied by those antecedents.
issues.evidence_needed: Verified primary sources for direct optimization/contraction and stochastic-recursion antecedents, plus either a proof of a substantive distinction/common result or appropriately registered empirical evidence for a practically relevant claim.

issues.observed_evidence: The introduction says the results have deliberately separate domains and that no theorem connects their state spaces or consequences. Future Work says no empirical policy or experiment is defined or evaluated. The limitations and conclusion repeat that no common formal model or empirical evidence is present; the claim map marks the only deployment claim C-DEPLOY-001 as planned rather than active evidence.
issues.why_it_matters: The paper provides neither a shared conceptual advance nor evidence that any scoped calculation resolves a consequential learning problem. Theory-only evaluation would be appropriate for a novel, useful theorem, but here the stated absence of both a connection and an application leaves three isolated calculations whose joint value is unsubstantiated.
issues.required_fix: Choose and substantiate one coherent contribution: for example, derive a nontrivial unifying theorem that materially extends the separate identities, or evaluate a pre-specified practical implication with claim-linked, reproducible evidence. Do not use an experiment to imply a transfer beyond its measured scope.
issues.verification_test: The revised abstract and introduction state one falsifiable central contribution, and its supporting theorem or experiment demonstrably links T1--T3 or establishes a clearly bounded practical consequence; the claim-evidence map contains all required source, configuration, and result links for any empirical claim.
issues.evidence_needed: A valid common formal model and proof, or a completed preregistered matched-path study with code/version, data/split hashes, configuration, seeds, outputs, and analysis registered for the active manuscript claim.

issues.observed_evidence: A substantial portion of the short main text discusses excluded historical material, absence of an experiment, and what the paper does not establish. issues.why_it_matters: The boundaries are necessary, yet the current allocation reinforces the impression of an audit artifact rather than helping readers evaluate a substantive contribution. This presentation issue is secondary to the missing contribution and cannot cure it alone.

issues.verification_test: A reader can state the motivating problem, the paper's one distinct contribution, and its relation to the closest theorem-level work from the abstract and introduction without relying on repeated non-claim disclaimers.

ethics_concerns: No active human-subject, dataset, deployment, or intervention study is reported. The manuscript's future-work boundary appropriately says a future policy must not use protected, test, or oracle labels at decision time (paper.tex:293--298).
llm_usage_disclosure: This review was produced by an isolated AI subagent for internal pre-submission quality control. I reviewed only the supplied frozen snapshot and rubric; it is not peer review and does not establish acceptance prospects.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: A verified, direct antecedent comparison showing a meaningful theorem-level distinction, together with a nontrivial theorem that unifies or materially extends the present scoped statements.

Alternatively, a completed and reproducible, claim-linked empirical study demonstrating a carefully bounded practical consequence, without asserting that T1--T3 automatically transfer to nonlinear SGD or neural networks.
A revised introduction and related-work section that state one falsifiable contribution and its exact boundary relative to direct prior work.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: A direct antecedent that already contains any purported new combined theorem or shows that the claimed distinction is only wording.
Any attempt to use the planned protocol or remote-only/historical results as active evidence without the required source, configuration, data, seed, output, and claim-level provenance links.
A counterexample to a displayed theorem within its printed assumptions.
review_limitations: The isolation boundary permitted review only of the frozen snapshot. I did not search external literature, so I cannot independently establish novelty or identify omitted direct antecedents beyond the snapshot's own admission that this comparison is unverified.
I assessed the self-contained proof steps and supplied provenance records but did not execute new experiments or inspect unavailable raw historical/remote artifacts.
